title: Trapping Rain Water
summary: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map with each bar having a width of 1, calculate the total volume of water that can be trapped after a rainfall.
statement: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map with each bar having a width of 1, calculate the total volume of water that can be trapped after a rainfall.
hints: Water at one index is limited by the smaller of the best walls on its two sides.
Track maximum walls seen from both ends; the smaller wall determines which side can be finalized.
Advance the side with smaller known maximum. Update that maximum and add the difference between it and the current bar.
Each index contributes a nonnegative depth exactly once.
editorial: The depth above an index is the smaller of its highest left and right barriers minus its own height, clipped at zero. Scan inward with the highest barrier seen from each end. When one known barrier is smaller, the opposite known barrier already suffices to bound that side, so its contribution is final. Moving each pointer inward once gives linear time and constant extra space.

tests.explanation: The trapped depths at indices 2,4,5,6,9 are 1,1,2,1,1, totaling 6.
The internal depths are 2,4,1,2; their sum is 9.
